skill.name: antfu
skill.description: Apply Anthony Fu's opinionated JavaScript and TypeScript conventions for project setup, linting, Vue/Nuxt apps, monorepos, and library publishing.
skill.summary: Apply Anthony Fu's JavaScript, TypeScript, linting, monorepo, and library conventions.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious code was found. Most static alerts are Markdown or configuration examples, but package-manager execution guidance and unpinned third-party GitHub Actions workflows create real review risks.

remediation.issue: Package-manager commands can execute project scripts or downloaded packages.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running ni, nr, nlx, npx, or pnpm commands. Show the command and working directory first.

remediation.issue: Reusable GitHub Actions workflows are pinned to a mutable main branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin third-party workflows to reviewed commit SHAs or trusted version tags, especially release workflows with write or OIDC permissions.

remediation.issue: Automatic lint fixes and Git hooks can modify repository files.
remediation.suggestion: Check the working tree before running fix commands, and summarize changed files after execution.

content.value_statement: Modern JavaScript projects often need consistent tooling decisions. This skill applies Anthony Fu style guidance for linting, setup, apps, monorepos, and libraries.
actual_capabilities: Recommends TypeScript organization patterns, including separated types, constants, and explicit return types.
Configures @antfu/eslint-config with framework options, formatters, overrides, and VS Code settings.
Guides Vue, Nuxt, UnoCSS, and Storybook conventions for application projects.
Outlines pnpm workspace, catalog, alias, and Turborepo patterns for monorepos.
Suggests tsdown, ESM exports, API snapshots, and prepack scripts for libraries.
Provides setup examples for .gitignore, GitHub Actions, and VS Code extensions.
limitations: It reflects Anthony Fu's preferences, not universal project standards.
It may suggest package-manager commands that require user review before execution.
It does not verify third-party workflow security or package integrity.
It does not replace framework documentation for version-specific behavior.

use_cases.title: Start a TypeScript project
use_cases.description: Set baseline linting, TypeScript, editor, and project structure choices before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize a monorepo
use_cases.description: Align workspace scripts, aliases, catalogs, and task orchestration across several packages.

use_cases.title: Prepare a library release
use_cases.description: Use pure ESM packaging, tsdown builds, API snapshots, and prepack safeguards for npm publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Set up a new app
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a new Vite Vue app using Anthony Fu conventions. Include linting, TypeScript, and basic project files.

prompt_templates.title: Configure linting
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure @antfu/eslint-config for this existing Vue project. Explain required packages and VS Code settings.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a package
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this TypeScript package to a pure ESM library. Use tsdown, API snapshots, and stable package exports.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a monorepo
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this monorepo against Anthony Fu conventions. Propose changes for aliases, pnpm workspaces, scripts, catalogs, and CI workflows.

output_examples.input: Create a new TypeScript library package.
output: Recommends pure ESM output with tsdown.
Adds API snapshot testing to protect public exports.
Suggests prepack build safeguards before publishing.

output_examples.input: Bring a Vue app in line with Anthony Fu preferences.
output: Chooses explicit imports and disables new auto-imports.
Uses UnoCSS and Storybook guidance for component work.

output_examples.input: Review a pnpm workspace for consistency.
output: Checks workspace layout and recursive scripts.
Recommends centralized aliases only when already configured.
Reviews catalog names and CI workflow choices.

best_practices: Confirm the target project type before applying app, library, or monorepo guidance.
Review every generated command before running it in a user repository.
Pin external CI workflows and dependencies according to the project's security policy.
anti_patterns: Applying all conventions to an existing project without checking current tooling.
Running package-manager commands without confirming the package name and working directory.
Replacing project-specific architecture decisions with this style guide.

faq.question: Is this skill official Anthony Fu guidance?
faq.answer: It is a community-packaged skill based on Anthony Fu style and tooling references.

faq.question: Does it replace Prettier?
faq.answer: @antfu/eslint-config can handle formatting, so many projects do not need Prettier separately.

faq.question: Can it create Vue and Nuxt projects?
faq.answer: It can guide project setup and conventions, but the user should approve dependency installation commands.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pnpm workspace, alias, catalog, and optional Turborepo guidance.

faq.question: Can it help publish npm libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers tsdown, pure ESM packages, exports, API snapshots, and prepack scripts.

faq.question: What should users review before applying it?
faq.answer: Users should review package-manager commands, GitHub Actions references, and any file changes before execution.
